# Request pipeline, middleware and filters

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `aspnet-request-pipeline` · **ASP.NET Core & API Engineering** · Catalog level: foundation

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S02-Q001](#S02-Q001)

<p>What is middleware in ASP.NET Core, and how does one request pass through a middleware pipeline?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Trace an HTTP request through the chosen ASP.NET Core/MVC pipeline and defend where a shared concern belongs.</p>

<ul>
<li>Explain request and response control flow, including early termination.</li>
<li>Connect routing, identity, permissions and error handling to their required context.</li>
<li>Choose middleware or an MVC filter from lifecycle coverage.</li>
<li>Use a trace or focused test to investigate a misplaced component.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>Start with middleware as a request-processing boundary. Routing and MVC lifecycle questions identify where endpoint and action context become available; implementation and ordering questions use that context to explain behavior. Failure questions test the boundary, then the middleware/filter comparison and end-to-end trace turn it into a defensible production choice. Clarify the MVC family and version before using lifecycle details.</p>

### S02-Q001 · Foundation

<p>What is middleware in ASP.NET Core, and how does one request pass through a middleware pipeline?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q001](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q001)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q001](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q001)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What is middleware and how does the middleware pipeline work?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the pipeline as a sequence of components handling an HTTP request and response. Make the control flow visible rather than listing built-in components.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Trace responsibility and control flow through a bounded request pipeline.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a named ASP.NET Core version and hosting setup; consult official documentation before relying on registration conventions.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Draw a normal path and a path that ends before the endpoint.</li>
<li>Explain which components can observe the response and propose an ordering test.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Describing middleware as a list of unrelated helpers without tracing a request.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you demonstrate that one component stops the remaining pipeline?</li>
<li>What changes when a component throws before calling the next component?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q005 · Mechanism

<p>What is an MVC action filter, and what kind of responsibility belongs at that point in request processing?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q005](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q005)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q005](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q005)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What are action filters and when should they be used?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the action boundary and the context the filter needs. Use one concern to distinguish filter behavior from business logic inside the action.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain an action-filter responsibility and its lifecycle boundary.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use ASP.NET Core MVC, naming the version and synchronous or asynchronous filter API; consult official lifecycle documentation.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace the action and filter interactions for one request.</li>
<li>Identify what the filter should leave to application logic and test an interrupted action.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Putting unrelated business workflows into a filter because it runs around actions.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you prevent the filter from executing a concern twice?</li>
<li>What can you observe if the action never runs?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q007 · Mechanism

<p>How does MVC routing select the endpoint or action for an incoming URL?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q007](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q007)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q007](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q007)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain MVC routing.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain how a request is matched to executable behavior. Distinguish route matching from the later use of route values as action inputs.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Trace endpoint selection and diagnose an unmatched or ambiguous route.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify ASP.NET Core MVC versus older ASP.NET MVC; state version, attribute or conventional routing, and check official rules.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Walk through one route table and matching request.</li>
<li>Compare an unmatched request with an ambiguous match using observable evidence.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating routing as string concatenation or assuming route matching validates every input.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you test two routes whose patterns overlap?</li>
<li>Which part of your explanation changes between attribute and conventional routing?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q008 · Mechanism

<p>Explain the lifecycle of one MVC request that renders a page, from route selection to the final response.</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q008](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q008)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q008](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q008)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain the MVC request/page lifecycle.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Identify the chosen model, action and rendering responsibilities. The source wording says request/page lifecycle, so clarify the framework instead of mixing MVC with an unrelated page model.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Build a coherent lifecycle trace for a specified MVC application.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Declare ASP.NET Core MVC or older ASP.NET MVC and its version; do not assume a Web Forms or Razor Pages lifecycle. Check the applicable official lifecycle.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explain transitions using one request and the data available at each stage.</li>
<li>Trace what changes when validation fails or rendering throws.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Combining lifecycle stages from different frameworks into one sequence.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How does the trace differ when the action returns data instead of a view?</li>
<li>Where would you instrument a slow render?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q002 · Application

<p>How would you implement and register custom middleware for one clearly stated cross-cutting concern?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q002](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q002)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q002](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q002)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do you implement custom middleware?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Choose a small concern, such as measuring request duration, and explain its integration. A cross-cutting concern affects several endpoints rather than one business operation.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Turn a pipeline responsibility into an inspectable implementation design.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name the ASP.NET Core version and activation model; check official documentation for dependency lifetime and registration requirements.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Show the invocation boundary and intended response behavior.</li>
<li>Specify placement, dependency ownership and a test for a failing request.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Providing a code skeleton without explaining placement or dependency lifetime.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you test the middleware independently of a controller?</li>
<li>What happens if a dependency needs request-specific state?</li>
</ul>

### S02-Q003 · Failure cases

<p>How can middleware ordering change routing, authentication, authorization and exception handling for the same request?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q003](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q003)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q003](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q003)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How does middleware ordering affect routing, authentication, authorization and exception handling?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Authentication identifies a caller; authorization checks permission. Trace one request to explain why a component needs information or coverage from another component.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Diagnose pipeline-order failures through causal traces.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify the ASP.NET Core version, endpoint model and explicit or implicit registrations; verify ordering rules in official documentation.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Compare a working order with a failing order using the same request.</li>
<li>Show how endpoint metadata and an exception affect the observed response.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Reciting an order without explaining its dependencies or assuming all hosts register identically.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Which exception locations would your handler actually cover?</li>
<li>How would you isolate an authorization failure caused by ordering?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q009"></a>

### S02-Q009 · Failure cases

<p>How would you handle an unhandled API exception while preserving a useful client contract and diagnostic evidence?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q009](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q009)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q009](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q009)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do you handle unhandled exceptions in an API?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain who owns the error response and what operators need to investigate it. Separate unexpected failures from expected business errors without inventing a framework default.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design consistent failure reporting with explicit response boundaries.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify ASP.NET Core version, environment and whether the response has started; verify official exception-handling behavior.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace a failing dependency to its client-visible outcome and correlated log.</li>
<li>Explain response-started and information-disclosure limits, with a test for each.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Returning every exception detail to the caller or claiming one handler covers every failure.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you do if part of the response is already sent?</li>
<li>How would you avoid logging the same exception redundantly?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q004 · Trade-offs

<p>For a stated cross-cutting concern, when would you choose middleware and when would you choose an MVC filter?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q004](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q004)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q004](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q004)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare middleware and MVC filters.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare the information and lifecycle boundary each extension point needs. Keep the decision tied to a concrete concern instead of treating the two mechanisms as interchangeable.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose an extension point from required context and coverage.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Assume ASP.NET Core MVC controllers; establish the version and confirm documented boundaries before generalizing to other endpoint types.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explain the context required by the concern and where it becomes available.</li>
<li>Compare coverage and a failure case for each candidate.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Saying one mechanism replaces the other for every endpoint and concern.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Would the same choice cover a non-MVC endpoint?</li>
<li>What if the concern needs both action arguments and request-wide timing?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q006 · Production decision

<p>Draw one request from client through the API and application layer to a database or external dependency, then back to the client.</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q006](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q006)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q006](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q006)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Draw the end-to-end lifecycle of a request from client to API, application layer, database/external dependency and response.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Label responsibilities and the points where state or latency can change. Include one failed dependency call so the diagram explains observable behavior, not only architecture boxes.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Connect an end-to-end request trace to diagnostic evidence.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Choose one concrete operation and deployment; specify the ASP.NET Core version before relying on framework lifecycle details.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace success and failure with ownership at each boundary.</li>
<li>Identify evidence that separates application delay from dependency delay.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Drawing layers without data flow, response ownership or failure propagation.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Where would you correlate logs across the dependency boundary?</li>
<li>What would the client observe if the database commits but the response is lost?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>Agent-added production exercise: an API contains MVC controllers and one non-MVC endpoint. Add a shared duration log and investigate a controller request that unexpectedly receives an authorization error while another endpoint throws before responding. Draw success and failure traces, choose the extension points, and propose tests distinguishing a placement problem from a genuine permission denial. State the framework/version and verify its documented lifecycle.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Explains middleware, routing and filters and draws a plausible normal MVC request.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defends component placement using available context; traces termination and exception boundaries; proposes discriminating tests and states framework limits.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>An asserted order or diagram alone does not establish coverage. Need a relevant trace, focused tests, or an explicit documentation-backed verification plan.</p>
